jobs.title: Security Analyst
jobs.description: What You Can Expect Join Zoom's Security Operations Centre team in India, where your work directly shapes how we detect, respond to, and recover from threats across a complex, global technology environment. You'll operate at the intersection of SIEM engineering, incident response, and threat hunting, bringing analytical rigor to ambiguous situations and building the detection capabilities that keep Zoom secure. At this level, you're expected to lead investigations from triage through resolution, collaborate across cloud, identity, and product security disciplines, and continuously improve the processes and tooling that power our SOC. If you're energized by fast-moving threat landscapes and thrive in a team that values both depth of expertise and open collaboration, this role offers real scope to grow and make an impact. About the Team Our SOC India team sits at the heart of Zoom's global security operations, working alongside detection engineering, IT, cloud security, and product security teams to protect a platform trusted by hundreds of millions of people worldwide. The team covers the full spectrum of security events, from phishing and identity threats to cloud misconfigurations and product security incidents, operating with a follow-the-sun model. We value clear thinking, rigorous documentation, and a shared commitment to continuously strengthening Zoom's security posture. Responsibilities Monitor, triage, and investigate security alerts across SIEM, EDR, email security, identity, and cloud platforms using CrowdStrike NGSIEM, Splunk, and related tooling. Lead incident response from initial triage through containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review. Partner with the Incident Response team to address security incidents and provide timely support. Work proactively with Cyber Threat Intelligence to gather actionable intelligence and respond effectively to incidents. Collaborate closely with the Detection Engineering team to develop new detection and reduce false positives. Create, tune, and manage detection rules and alerts in CrowdStrike NGSIEM and Splunk, reducing false positives and maintaining clear documentation of logic and coverage. Apply AI tools to accelerate incident analysis, summarize investigations, and support detection development, validating all outputs before acting on them. Investigate phishing and email threats using Proofpoint, and analyze suspicious files and URLs through sandbox platforms such as Joe Sandbox. Investigate identity-based threats and suspicious authentication activity in Okta, and analyze cloud security events across AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI to identify misconfigurations and attacker behavior. Handle PSIRT cases related to product security, coordinating with engineering and cross-functional teams to assess impact and track remediation. Read and interpret PowerShell and Python scripts, and apply scripting and automation to streamline investigation, enrichment, and reporting workflows. Document incidents, detections, and playbooks to a standard that supports handover, audits, and continuous improvement, and contribute to shift handovers, metrics reporting, and SOC process improvements. What We're Looking For 3 to 6 years of hands-on experience in SOC operations, incident response, or threat hunting. Practical experience with CrowdStrike NGSIEM (Falcon Next-Gen SIEM) and CrowdStrike EDR, including detection rule development, alert tuning, and host-level investigation. Proficiency with Splunk SIEM, including writing searches, building alerts, and supporting detection engineering workflows. Experience investigating email threats with Proofpoint Email Security and analyzing suspicious files and URLs using sandbox environments such as Joe Sandbox. Hands-on experience with at least two cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, or OCI) from a security monitoring perspective, and experience investigating identity-based threats in Okta logs. Working knowledge of PowerShell and Python for security scripting and automation, with a strong understanding of attacker techniques mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Experience handling PSIRT cases or product security incidents, and strong written communication skills for incident documentation and stakeholder reporting. Ways of Working Our structured hybrid approach is centered around our offices and remote work environments. The work style of each role, Hybrid, Remote, or In-Person is indicated in the job description/posting. Benefits As part of our award-winning workplace culture and commitment to delivering happiness, our benefits program offers a variety of perks, benefits, and options to help employees maintain their physical, mental, emotional, and financial health; support work-life balance; and contribute to their community in meaningful ways. Click Learnfor more information. About Us Zoomies help people stay connected so they can get more done together. We set out to build the best collaboration platform for the enterprise, and today help people communicate better with products like Zoom Contact Center, Zoom Phone, Zoom Events, Zoom Apps, Zoom Rooms, and Zoom Webinars. We’re problem-solvers, working at a fast pace to design solutions with our customers and users in mind. Find room to grow with opportunities to stretch your skills and advance your career in a collaborative, growth-focused environment. Our Commitment At Zoom, we believe great work happens when people feel supported and empowered. We’re committed to fair hiring practices that ensure every candidate is evaluated based on skills, experience, and potential. If you require an accommodation during the hiring process, let us know—we’re here to support you at every step. If you need assistance navigating the interview process due to a medical disability, please submit an Accommodations Request Form and someone from our team will reach out soon. This form is solely for applicants who require an accommodation due to a qualifying medical disability. Non-accommodation-related requests, such as application follow-ups or technical issues, will not be addressed. Our interviews are supported by BrightHire, a tool that helps us create a consistent and thoughtful interview experience and may include recordings. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins. Why join Coupa? Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend. Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence. Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other. Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa. The Impact of an Associate Security Engineer at Coupa: Coupa's Security Engineers keep our enterprise, product, platform, and customer data safe. As an Associate Security Engineer, you'll build your foundation in cloud, application, and infrastructure security by contributing to real, well-scoped engineering work alongside experienced teammates. You'll partner with Engineering, IT, and Compliance, learn how we build durable, automated security tooling instead of one-off fixes, and grow your root-cause analysis skills with mentorship and regular feedback. This is a role for someone early in their security career who wants hands-on ownership of growing scope — with the support to get there. What You'll Do: Support the design and implementation of multi-cloud security controls — VPC segmentation, security groups/NACLs, and least-privilege IAM policies — on well-scoped tasks, with guidance from senior engineers. Build familiarity with permission boundaries and Organizations/SCPs along the way. Contribute to policy as code and IaC security guardrails in CI/CD pipelines: write and tune rules, reduce false positives, and help keep pre-merge and pre-deploy checks reliable. Assist in hardening containerized workloads and Kubernetes clusters, including image scanning, admission control, pod security standards, and network policies. Triage vulnerability findings from application packages, container images, and third-party dependencies. Gather context on exploitability and business impact, and escalate complex or ambiguous findings to senior teammates. Help the Risk & Compliance team gather technical evidence for audit frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP), and learn what auditable evidence looks like. Write and maintain scripts and small automations that make security work faster and more repeatable. Learn from mentors through pairing, design reviews, and feedback on your remediation plans. Document what you learn and help improve runbooks. Support the secure design, deployment, and operational monitoring of enterprise AI systems, models, and agentic workflows. Help design and develop internal AI-driven security tools, automation scripts, and guardrails to improve threat detection and vulnerability remediation. What You Will Bring to Coupa: 0–2 years of experience in security, cloud, DevOps, IT, or software engineering. Internships, co-ops, research, and hands-on personal or lab projects count. Foundational knowledge of cloud security concepts (AWS, GCP, or Azure) — IAM, networking, and common misconfigurations — gained through work, coursework, labs, or certifications. Working scripting skills in Python, Bash, or JavaScript, and interest in building or extending internal security tooling. Familiarity with vulnerability scanning concepts (dependency and container scanning). Exposure to CI/CD pipelines is a plus. Basic awareness of common compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) and a willingness to learn how they translate into technical controls. Curiosity and a habit of asking why — you want to understand the cause of a vulnerability, not just what the scanner reported. Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort asking questions, asking for help, and escalating early. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience (bootcamps, military, self-directed learning, or similar). Entry-level certifications are a plus: Security+, ISC2 CC, AWS Cloud Practitioner or AWS/GCP/Azure security certifications. The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. Business Travel Protection: Travel with peace of mind. Zurich Travel Assist provides medical, safety, pre-trip planning, and emergency support during any business travel . Referral Bonus Program: Share the Coupa experience! Receive generous monetary referral bonuses when you successfully refer talented friends or acquaintances who are hired into open roles . Please note: In addition to these global well-being perks, Coupa offers highly competitive, location-specific benefits packages (which include comprehensive medical/dental insurance, retirement/pension plans, and life or accident protection) tailored to your primary work location. We are not looking for someone to only advise us and leave the work to our team: you will do a large part of the security work yourself, working inside our repositories, pipelines and cloud accounts alongside our engineers. You will configure tools, fix and harden things, write the processes and documents, and run the sessions, while showing our team how it is done along the way. Our goal is a company that runs a secure development lifecycle on every project, has its own house in order, is well on the way to ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and has an internal Security Lead who can work with you and gradually take over day-to-day ownership. This is a part-time role. Responsibilities Assessment and governance Run the security maturity assessment yourself (for example OWASP SAMM), review our repositories, pipelines and cloud setup, and turn the findings into a prioritized roadmap. Write our core security policies and procedures: access control, acceptable use, secure development, incident response, vendor and AI tool usage. Set up and maintain the security backlog, risk register and progress metrics, and report progress to management monthly. Company security ("secure the house") Configure and enforce SSO and MFA across email, Git hosting, cloud consoles, CI/CD and Passbolt. Review and fix access rights, and set up onboarding and offboarding checklists. Harden our Passbolt setup and implement a secrets manager for applications and pipelines, including migrating existing secrets out of code and CI variables. Implement baseline hardening for laptops, cloud accounts, backups and logging. Write the incident response plan and run tabletop exercises with the team. Secure software development Build our standard Secure SDLC, based on OWASP ASVS and OWASP SAMM, and roll it out on real client projects. Configure and tune our SecOps platform: reduce false positives, set up pipeline quality gates and triage findings together with the teams. Add the missing scanning to our CI/CD pipelines yourself: SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, IaC and container scanning, DAST and SBOM generation. Run threat modeling sessions on active projects and document the results. Do security code reviews of high-risk changes and help developers fix vulnerabilities. Perform internal security testing of our applications before releases, and scope and coordinate external penetration tests. Regulation and compliance Map how the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), NIS2 and relevant local regulations affect us and our clients. Write and implement our vulnerability handling and disclosure process, including support for clients' CRA reporting obligations. Do the hands-on ISO/IEC 27001 preparation work: scope, risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, policies and evidence, and work with the certification body. Client offering Help define security service tiers we can include in client proposals. Fill in client security questionnaires and build a reusable answer set. Run short internal workshops on key topics (for example OWASP Top 10, threat modeling, secure CI/CD). Recommend training and certification paths for developers, Security Champions and DevOps engineers. Comfortable doing the work yourself: configuring security tools, writing pipeline configuration, reviewing code, testing applications and writing policies. Practical experience setting up a secure development lifecycle and integrating security tools into CI/CD pipelines. Good knowledge of cloud security in at least one major cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP). Ability to explain security risks in plain language to both engineers and management. Fluent English, written and spoken. Kubernetes and container security experience. Knowledge of security risks in AI and LLM-based applications. Nice to have Experience with the EU Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2 and GDPR in a software vendor or supplier context. Experience building security offerings for clients in an agency or outsourcing environment. Experience implementing or auditing ISO/IEC 27001 (or a comparable framework such as SOC 2). Certifications (one or more preferred) Hands-on certifications such as OSCP, BSCP, CDP or CKS ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor Cloud security certification (AWS Security Specialty, AZ-500 or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer) CISSP, CISM or CSSLP The Secret Ingredients That Make Us Special: Your growth is our growth. We invest in your future with paid training and other professional opportunities. We're industry innovators at the forefront of change. Equipped with the latest technologies and a team of knowledgeable colleagues by your side, you'll embrace new and interesting challenges. Your location. Your schedule. Pick your time zone, choose your preferred hours, and work from the place where you feel most at home. Flexibility and freedom are in our DNA! As long as you have a stable internet connection and the drive to thrive, you can travel and work from anywhere you like. A workload you can rely on. We'll set you enough tasks to keep that mind busy! At Scopic , we'll ensure you always have a consistent flow of engaging, challenging work to do. Recognition and reward. We acknowledge diligence and hard work through annual pay increases for good performance. Down to Business! Your starting rate is negotiable depending on your skills and experience. This is an hourly paid position. Contractors are paid monthly via wire transfer. Our Values: Scopic is an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, marital status, national origin, gender, veteran status, sexual orientation, age, or disability status. Have the skills, the drive, and the passion to join the Scopic family? Apply today to join our growing team of remote professionals from around the world. jobs.title: SOC Analyst (04:00–13:00 UTC)
jobs.description: About the job The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus. Responsibilities Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms. Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout. Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures. Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions. Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock. Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK. Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage. Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization. Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks. Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations. Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment. Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats. Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus. Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles. Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail. Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely. Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones. About You You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment. jobs.description: About the role You’ll be the engineer our managed services clients rely on when something looks wrong in their AWS accounts or on their endpoints, and the one who makes sure it doesn’t happen twice.You will run AWS-native security services and enterprise EDR/XDR platforms across many client environments, lead incident response from the first alert to the root cause, manage devices through Microsoft Intune, and keep the controls and evidence clients need for SOC 2. The stack you’ll own: Five layers, many client environments. These are the services and tools you’ll work with every week. AWS foundation Accounts, identity, encryption and network edges AWS Organizations & SCPs Control Tower IAM & IAM Identity Center IAM Access Analyzer KMS Secrets Manager VPC & Network Firewall AWS WAF & Shield Cloud workloads EC2, containers and serverless, protected by AWS-native and thirdparty tools CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security Trend Micro Vision One / Cloud One Workload Security Bitdefender GravityZone Amazon Inspector GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring Systems Manager Patch Manager ECR image scanning Amazon EKS Endpoints, mobile and email Laptops, servers, phones and the mailboxes people use on them CrowdStrike Falcon SentinelOne Singularity Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Bitdefender GravityZone Microsoft Intune Intune app protection (MAM) Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access Microsoft Defender for Office 365 SPF, DKIM & DMARC Detection and response EDR, XDR and MDR working as one service Amazon GuardDuty AWS Security Hub Amazon Detective AWS Security Incident Response Microsoft Sentinel Microsoft Defender XDR MDR partners Compliance and evidence Proof that controls work, ready for auditors SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria AWS Config conformance packs AWS Audit Manager AWS CloudTrail CIS Benchmarks Key responsibilities: AWS cloud security Design and run a multi-account security architecture for each client: a dedicated security tooling account with delegated administration for GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Macie and Detective, and an organization-wide CloudTrail delivered to a locked-down log archive account. Enable and tune GuardDuty protection plans (S3, EKS, Runtime Monitoring, Malware Protection, RDS and Lambda), maintain suppression rules, and route findings by severity to the right queue and on-call engineer. nClouds : Cloud Security Engineer Page 2 of 7 Operate Security Hub with central configuration across the organization: enable standards (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, CIS, PCI DSS and NIST SP800-53), build automation rules and custom insights, and keep findings deduplicated. Own identity security: IAM Identity Center permission sets, service control and resource control policies, permission boundaries, cross-account role trust reviews, root account protection, MFA enforcement, access key rotation, and IAM Access Analyzer findings for external and unused access. Protect data with KMS key policies and rotation, S3 Block Public Access and bucket policy reviews, default EBS and RDS encryption, Secrets Manager rotation and Macie sensitive data discovery. Harden networks through security group and NACL reviews, AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoints, WAF managed and rate-based rules, Shield Advanced and VPC Flow Log analysis. Secure containers and serverless: EKS cluster hardening, EKS Pod Identity or IRSA, Kubernetes RBAC and audit logs, ECR enhanced scanning, and least-privilege Lambda execution roles. Build auto-remediation for common risks, such as public S3 buckets, security groups open to the internet on SSH or RDP, disabled logging and exposed access keys, using AWS Config rules, EventBridge, Lambda and Systems Manager Automation. Centralize security logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS, WAF and load balancer logs) in Amazon Security Lake or the client’s SIEM, with retention set to meet compliance needs. Run security posture reviews against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and the Well-Architected Security pillar, then drive remediation with the client. Review Terraform and CloudFormation changes for security misconfigurations before they reach production. Third-party cloud and workload security on AWS Deploy and manage third-party cloud security platforms alongside AWS-native services, including CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security, Trend Micro Vision One and Bitdefender GravityZone, covering workload protection, cloud posture (CSPM) and container security. Onboard client AWS organizations to these platforms with least-privilege cross-account IAM roles, deployed at scale through CloudFormation StackSets or Terraform, and monitor connector health so no account drops out of coverage. Roll out and maintain sensors and agents on Linux and Windows EC2 instances, golden AMIs, Auto Scaling groups and EKS clusters using Systems Manager Distributor and State Manager, user data or Helm, and manage kernel compatibility and sensor upgrades. Configure workload protection policies covering anti-malware, IPS and virtual patching, integrity monitoring, log inspection, application control and host firewall, tuned so production performance isn’t affected. Choose between agent-based and agentless (snapshot) scanning for each workload type, and explain the coverage trade-offs of each. Correlate and deduplicate findings between AWS-native and third-party tools, forward them to Security Hub or the SIEM, and agree a single source of truth per control to avoid overlap and alert fatigue. nClouds : Cloud Security Engineer Page 3 of 7 Reconcile EC2 and EKS inventory against each tool’s console every month to catch unprotected instances, stale agents and licensing gaps. Advise clients on where AWS-native services are enough and where a third-party tool is needed, and run migrations between tools without losing coverage. Endpoint and EDR/XDR administration Administer EDR/XDR platforms, including CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR, Trend Micro Vision One and Bitdefender GravityZone: sensor rollout and health, device groups, response actions and integrations. Publish regular agent coverage reports so no unprotected laptop, server or workload goes unnoticed. Laptop, mobile and email protection Handle malware detections end to end: confirm the alert, kill or quarantine the threat, isolate the device if needed, remove persistence, confirm the device is clean, and restore, roll back or reimage where required. Contain ransomware on endpoints quickly using EDR isolation and rollback features, and work with backup owners on recovery. Triage reported and detected phishing, business email compromise and malicious attachments or links: trace the message, purge it from every mailbox, block the sender, domain or URL, and reset and review any compromised account. Manage Windows, macOS, iOS and Android devices in Microsoft Intune: enrollment (Windows Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment, Android Enterprise), compliance policies, configuration profiles, BitLocker and FileVault encryption, Defender onboarding and Conditional Access with Microsoft Entra ID. Protect personal (BYOD) devices with Intune app protection policies, and handle lost or stolen devices with remote lock, selective wipe or full wipe. Enforce device control for USB and removable media, application control, web content filtering, browser and extension policies, and OS and third-party app patching through Intune. Security policy design and audits Write, configure and maintain the security policies inside each tool: EDR prevention and detection policies, Defender attack surface reduction rules, Intune compliance, configuration and app protection policies, Conditional Access, email protection policies, cloud workload policies in CrowdStrike, Trend Micro and Bitdefender, and AWS SCPs and Security Hub standards. Build and maintain nClouds ’ standard policy baseline for each tool, keep it under version and change control, and apply it consistently when onboarding new clients. Audit policy configuration across client tenants on a regular schedule against that baseline, vendor recommendations, CIS Benchmarks and the client’s own standards, and flag drift, gaps, disabled protections and overly broad exclusions. Review exclusion and exception requests, document the risk and approval, and set a review date for each one. Draft the security policy documents that back these configurations (endpoint security, mobile device, email security, acceptable use and incident response), and turn audit findings into client reports and SOC 2 evidence. nClouds : Cloud Security Engineer Page 4 of 7 Detection, MDR and incident response Triage and investigate escalated alerts from GuardDuty, Security Hub, Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR and EDR consoles; separate real threats from noise quickly and record the reasoning. Lead incident response end to end following NIST SP800-61: scope affected accounts and hosts, contain (isolate endpoints, disable or rotate credentials, quarantine IAM access keys, snapshot volumes for forensics), eradicate, recover and write the RCA. Use AWS Security Incident Response for case management, triage and containment on AWS, and work alongside MDR partners and client security teams during active incidents. Write and tune detections mapped to MITRE ATT&CK in KQL, CloudWatch Logs Insights and Athena, reducing false positives without opening detection gaps. Automate repeatable response with EventBridge, Lambda, Step Functions, Systems Manager and Sentinel playbooks. This is a hands-on engineering position, not a general IT cybersecurity, SOC, network security or compliance-only role. Key Responsibilities 1. Embedded Product Security Architecture Design and implement security architectures for Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP and other embedded platforms. Perform device-level threat modeling, attack-surface analysis and security risk assessments. Identify threats involving physical device access, debug interfaces, firmware extraction, communication interfaces and software vulnerabilities. Translate security requirements into practical technical controls and engineering tasks. Collaborate with hardware, BSP, platform and application engineers to implement security by design. 2. Secure Boot, Device Identity and Cryptography Implement and validate Secure Boot, Verified Boot and chain-of-trust mechanisms. Work with hardware-backed security technologies such as TPM, HSM, secure elements, ARM TrustZone and OP-TEE, as applicable. Design secure device identity, key provisioning, key storage and key lifecycle mechanisms. Implement cryptographic signing, integrity verification and secure firmware authentication. Support secure manufacturing provisioning and device lifecycle security. 3. Embedded Linux and Android Platform Hardening Implement security controls within Embedded Linux and, where applicable, Android/AOSP platforms. Harden bootloaders, Linux kernels, operating-system configurations and device services. Work with Linux security mechanisms such as SELinux, AppArmor, dm-verity, dm-crypt and filesystem protection. Reduce attack surfaces by securing services, ports, permissions, interfaces and debug capabilities. Collaborate with Yocto/BSP engineers to integrate security controls into production firmware images. 4. Secure Firmware Updates and Product Lifecycle Security Design and implement secure firmware and OTA update mechanisms. Ensure firmware authenticity, integrity, rollback protection and secure recovery. Support secure update architectures for connected and field-deployed products. Investigate product vulnerabilities and contribute to remediation across supported software versions. Work with CVE databases, software composition analysis and SBOM generation. Assess vulnerability exploitability and product-specific security impact. Support static analysis, dynamic analysis, firmware analysis and penetration-testing activities. Develop or integrate security verification into CI/CD pipelines. Document security findings, remediation actions and verification evidence. 6. Contribute to product-security documentation and technical security decisions. Independently investigate and resolve complex embedded security issues. Required Qualifications and Experience Strong professional experience in embedded software engineering, with substantial hands-on responsibility for embedded product cybersecurity. Professional experience securing consumer electronics, medical devices or comparable connected embedded products. Strong understanding of embedded hardware, firmware, bootloaders, operating systems and device security boundaries. Hands-on experience implementing security controls in Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP or comparable embedded platforms. Demonstrated practical experience in several of the following: Secure Boot, Verified Boot or hardware root of trust. Secure key storage, provisioning and cryptographic integration. Embedded Linux security hardening. Secure firmware updates and rollback protection. Device-level threat modeling and attack-surface reduction. Embedded vulnerability analysis and remediation. Strong Linux debugging and embedded systems troubleshooting skills. Proficiency in C/C++ and scripting with Python or Bash. Ability to independently own technical security tasks from design through implementation and verification. Experience working with cross-functional product-development teams. Preferred Qualifications Direct experience with consumer electronics , connected devices, smart home products, multimedia devices, wearables or other commercially deployed embedded products. Experience developing or securing medical-device software , connected medical equipment or regulated healthcare products. Practical experience with ARM TrustZone, OP-TEE, TPM, secure elements or hardware security modules. Experience with Yocto/OpenEmbedded, U-Boot, Linux kernel configuration and BSP security integration. Android Verified Boot (AVB), Android security architecture or SELinux policy development. Secure OTA frameworks and firmware-signing infrastructure. Experience with SBOM tooling, CVE assessment and software composition analysis. Familiarity with applicable product-security standards and guidance, such as IEC 62443, ETSI EN 303 645, IEC 81001-5-1, IEC 62304, ISO 14971 or relevant EU Cyber Resilience Act requirements. Experience supporting security verification, technical documentation and product-security audits. Experience working on products requiring long-term security maintenance and vulnerability response. What We Are Looking For We are particularly interested in engineers who can demonstrate: Security mechanisms they have personally designed, implemented, integrated or validated . Experience working with actual embedded products rather than security concepts alone. Understanding of how hardware, firmware, operating systems and connectivity affect device security. Ability to investigate vulnerabilities and implement practical remediation. Ownership of technical decisions and security deliverables. Clear communication with embedded engineering and product teams. Important: This position requires practical embedded product-security engineering experience. General IT security, SOC operations, infrastructure security, penetration testing without embedded-product engineering, or compliance-only experience will not independently meet the role requirements. Why Join L4B Software ? Work on embedded platform and product-security engineering challenges. Contribute to secure software platforms used in complex connected products. Work in an environment where technical depth, independent problem-solving and engineering quality matter. Application Please share your resume highlighting the embedded products and platforms you have worked on, the security mechanisms you personally implemented, and your experience with production or commercially deployed devices. Candidates will be assessed on demonstrated technical capabilities and alignment with the requirements of the role. ﻿﻿ Originally posted on Himalayas
